title: Do LLMs have a Gender (Entropy) Bias?

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4.2: 'Each of the questions is sent to each LLM (ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, ChatGPT-4-turbo, Llama3, and Deepseek-R1)'; Alg. 1: 'models←[chatgpt-3.5-turbo, chatgpt-4-turbo, llama3, deepseek-r1]'

prompt.location: Algorithm 1 (system prompt template 'Assistant gives recommendations to users on the <category> choices for their needs.' + user question); questions in the HF dataset
prompt.note: temperature 1, other hyperparameters default, each question in a fresh context, 1-minute delay between calls.

claim.metric: Welch t-statistic (p) male vs female Shannon entropy, Education category, 1 iteration
claim.location: Table 4, row ChatGPT-4-turbo, Education Recommendations, Shannon Entropy column (t=2.00, p=0.04)

data.source: RealWorldQuestioning benchmark, https://huggingface.co/datasets/SonalPrabhune/RealWorldQuestioning (Education: 79 questions x 2 gender variants; 434 x 2 overall)

notes: Temperature-1 sampling makes the t-statistic noisy and p=0.04 is unlikely to replicate exactly, but the pipeline (prompt, data, entropy metric) is fully specified. Whole-dataset re-run (870 questions x 3 seeds, long outputs) would be ~2,600 calls (high). Table 6 uses ChatGPT-4o (unpinned) as judge and is secondary.
